title: Feijoada
subtitle: Brazilian black bean stew with chorizo and pork belly
excerpt: Black beans slow-cooked with chorizo and pork belly in a smoky, garlicky broth with orange. Brazil's national dish is rich, deeply savoury and gets better the longer it sits. Serve with rice and sliced orange.
sourceNotes: Feijoada is considered the national dish of Brazil and is traditionally cooked on Saturdays for a slow family lunch. It has African and Portuguese roots from the colonial period.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes very well. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat gently on the hob.
recipe.batchNotes: This is a natural batch cook dish. Double the quantities easily.

content.text: Frying the garlic and onion in the chorizo fat before adding the beans is key. The rendered fat carries the smoked paprika flavour through the whole stew.
Place the chorizo and pork belly in a cold stockpot. Set over medium heat. Cook for 8 minutes until the fat renders and the chorizo colours.
Add the onion to the rendered fat. Cook for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic, paprika and cumin. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the black beans, stock, bay leaves, orange juice and zest. Stir well.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 40 minutes. Stir occasionally.
Mash a spoonful of beans against the side of the pot to thicken the stew. Stir in.
Remove the bay leaves. Stir in the parsley. Taste and season. Serve with white rice and sliced orange.

items.symptom: Stew is too thin and soupy.
items.cause: Needs more reduction or beans not mashed.
items.fix: Mash more beans against the pot side and simmer 10 minutes more.

items.cause: 60 minutes is not quite enough for thick cubes.
items.fix: Cut into smaller 2cm pieces next time, or extend cooking by 20 minutes.

items.cause: Chorizo and stock are both salty.
items.fix: Use low-salt stock; add a squeeze of orange juice to balance.
